record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop a mathematically firm microscopic theory of quantum non-equilibrium statistical mechanics near equilibrium, including rigorous treatments of the Kubo formula, the Joule effect, and transport theory more generally.

evidence.quote: We remark that the quantum non-equilibrium statistical mechanics remain a widely open subject. An important long term goal for constructive theory should be... to put on a firm mathematical microscopic analysis the Kubo formula and the Joule effect, and more generally transport theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a mathematically rigorous microscopic theory of quantum non-equilibrium statistical mechanics in the near-equilibrium (linear response) regime. Concretely, starting from a microscopic quantum many-body Hamiltonian model (e.g. a system of fermions on a lattice or in the continuum coupled to one or more thermal reservoirs at inverse temperatures β and chemical potentials μ, possibly perturbed by an external time-dependent driving field), establish the following:

1. Kubo formula. For a system initially in a Gibbs (KMS) state at inverse temperature β, perturbed by a small external field switched on adiabatically, prove that in the thermodynamic limit the induced expectation value of a current observable J is given, to first order in the field strength, by
   ⟨J⟩(t) = ∫ χ(t−s) F(s) ds + o(F),
 where the response kernel χ is expressed as an equilibrium correlation function of currents in the unperturbed dynamics, and identify the resulting transport coefficients (electrical, thermal, etc.) as well-defined limits.

2. Joule effect. Prove rigorously that, under a sustained external electric field, the system dissipates energy into the reservoirs at a rate equal to σ |E|² + o(|E|²), where σ is the conductivity obtained from the Kubo formula above, and that this dissipation manifests as a strictly positive entropy production rate.

3. Transport theory. More generally, derive from microscopic quantum dynamics the macroscopic transport equations governing the slow evolution of conserved quantities (charge, energy, momentum), including a rigorous proof of the existence of nontrivial transport coefficients and of Onsager reciprocity relations, in a class of interacting quantum many-body systems.

Provide such a theory with full mathematical rigor (existence of dynamics in infinite volume, well-defined non-equilibrium steady states, controlled thermodynamic and adiabatic limits) for at least one nontrivial interacting quantum model.
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous derivations of Kubo formulas and transport coefficients exist for some restricted settings (e.g. non-interacting electrons, quantum Hall systems by Bachmann–De Roeck–Fraas–Giuliani–Monaco–Porta and others, and certain spin chains), but a general mathematically firm microscopic theory of quantum non-equilibrium statistical mechanics covering the Kubo formula, Joule heating, and transport for genuinely interacting many-body systems remains broadly open and is widely cited as a major program in mathematical physics.

status_evidence.title: Adiabatic theorem and linear response for interacting fermions
status_evidence.snippet: We give a rigorous derivation of Kubo's formula for the linear response of interacting fermionic systems on the lattice in the gapped case.
status_evidence.claim: Kubo formula proven rigorously only in restricted (gapped, lattice fermion) settings, indicating the general program is still open.

status_evidence.title: Non-equilibrium statistical mechanics of open quantum systems (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Despite considerable progress, a complete microscopic theory of quantum transport and the Joule effect for general interacting systems remains an outstanding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: General quantum non-equilibrium statistical mechanics is still considered open.
